newsitem.title: GREECE: Clinton to visit Greece and Turkey - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Clinton to visit Greece and Turkey - newspaper.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton plans to visit Athens and Ankara next June to promote closer relations between uneasy neighbours Greece and Turkey, an Athens newspaper said on Sunday, quoting White House sources

The daily Kathimerini said Washington would push the two countries to agree on ways of settling their disputes before Clinton's visit and that his presence would underline the U.S. interest in stability in the southern Balkans.

"The first months of 1997 will be months of intense activity for the the Aegean and Cyprus issues. The visit will come either after progress has been achieved or as the start of a new effort in case the impasse continues," Kathimerini said.

The two countries, despite being NATO allies, almost went to war in January over disputed, uninhabited islets in the Aegean Sea. The United States stepped in to broker a deal which eased the tension but Greek-Turkish relations remain on a tightrope.
"Mr Clinton wants to show his personal interest in the eastern Mediterranean and Greek-Turkish relations," the paper's Washington correspondent Alexis Papahelas said, quoting a White House official.
Greek government officials could not be reached to comment on the report but government spokesman Dimitris Reppas has said Athens awaits a new U.S. initiative.
Athens and Ankara are at odds over territorial rights in the Aegean Sea, dotted with thousands of islands, and over the divided island of Cyprus.
